description: Shape 0 (n=32 b20, ~150us) is the run's most OVERHEAD-BOUND term and the geomean is SCALE-FREE, so a 2x cut there (~150->75us) moves the geomean ~5.5% (~39350->~37200, past #5 msaroufim 38304 and #4 revolutionaryspaces 37321). Leaders prove it winnable ('submission_eigh_n32_parallel'). brief-12 REFUTED custom KERNELS for n=32 (batched Jacobi/Householder-QL etc -- all occupancy-bound: batch=20 fills only ~6% of 148 SMs, unhidable latency), but its OWN conclusion was that cuSOLVER's ~150us is dominated by HOST dispatch/launch overhead and 'the win is minimizing OUR total launches + host ops' -- which it never actually implemented. Attack THAT directly (distinct mechanism from brief-12): CUDA-GRAPH capture (torch.cuda.CUDAGraph / make_graphed_callables) of the per-shape n=32 pipeline replayed across the benchmark's repeated same-shape calls, ELIMINATING per-op launch latency; plus preallocated persistent output/scratch buffers and fused elementwise (sort/gather) to cut host ops. Measure whether the n=32 path (and n<=64 generally) is graph-capturable end-to-end (the per-matrix residual-gate + cuSOLVER fallback are data-dependent -> may block capture; if so, capture only the capturable prefix, or use a fixed no-fallback path for the tiny well-behaved n=32 case gated by a cheap upfront check). Also try the same graph/preallocation lever on shapes 1 (n176) & 2 (n352) if it helps. PURE-TORCH (no nvcc) -- GPU-light amid briefs 21/22's heavy builds. Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback stays the correctness floor; no 'stream' substring; do not regress any shape. Forks best 4c1e8876.

CUDA-graph-replayed batched-Jacobi n=32 path, forced route (n<=64). Captures a pure-torch tournament-pairing Jacobi (6 sweeps) into a CUDA graph replayed per benchmark call; persistent I/O buffers; residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback OUTSIDE the graph. Fixed a device-side OOB assert by retaining the graph's index tensors + eye in the cache (else gc-freed after capture -> corrupt indices on replay). Validated 39/39, kernelguard CLEAN. shape0 n=32=22011.5us vs baseline 165us (133x REGRESSION); other 12 shapes unchanged. geomean 57553.504us vs parent 39535us. Root cause (nsys): cuSOLVER n=32 is 92% GPU kernel execution (105us batch_parallel_jacobi_algo1), NOT launch overhead, so graphing launches away cannot beat it -- the pure-torch Jacobi's own execution is ~22ms. cuSOLVER eigh itself is NOT graph-capturable (internal host sync -> capture invalidated, measured).

Self-timing gate for the n=32 CUDA-graph path (no-regression final state). Replaces the forced route with a one-time per-(n,b) MEASUREMENT of graph-Jacobi vs cuSOLVER on the live input class; caches the verdict; takes the graph path only on a >5% win. Same measured-faster-only philosophy as the rest of the router -> cannot regress. shape0 n=32=161.5us == baseline ~165us (gate correctly kept cuSOLVER). geomean 39458.266us vs parent 39535us (this run) -- within noise, no regression. Validated 39/39. VERDICT on the brief mechanism: graph capture of the n=32 pipeline is correct + kills launch latency but LOSES because (1) cuSOLVER eigh is NOT graph-capturable (internal host sync -> capture invalidated) and (2) nsys shows n=32 cuSOLVER is 92% GPU kernel EXECUTION (105us batch_parallel_jacobi_algo1 on b20, occupancy-bound), NOT the host/launch overhead the brief hypothesized; a capturable pure-torch eigh's own execution is ~22ms. The graph machinery is live + kernelguard CLEAN, retained for any (n,b) where it would win.

Explored the CUDA-graph mechanism on n=32 (primary) and n=176/352 (secondary). FINAL committed state = trial 2 (935201bb8): self-timing gate, geomean 39458us == parent (no regression), 39/39 valid, kernelguard CLEAN.

MEASURED FINDINGS (all built + benched live, not paper):
- n=32 cuSOLVER eigh is NOT graph-capturable: capture is invalidated by an internal host sync (tried default/relaxed/double backends). Confirmed by direct probe.
- nsys of the n=32 path (brief-23-probe-n32-parent + trial-2 profiles): 92% of the 165us/call is ONE GPU kernel executing -- batch_parallel_jacobi_algo1<...32,32,16> at 105us on b20 -- plus 5 satellite kernels ~9us. So ~114us is GPU EXECUTION and only ~40-50us is host/launch gap. This REFUTES the brief/brief-12 premise that ~150us is host-dispatch-dominated; it is occupancy-bound COMPUTE (b20 fills ~6% of 148 SMs, cuSOLVER runs 15 fixed Jacobi sweeps).
- A pure-torch capturable batched-Jacobi (tournament pairing, 6 sweeps) IS capturable and correct (0 bad / 50, eigen-res 1.9e-4 vs 1.6e-2 gate, ~100x margin) but its OWN execution is 22ms/call (index-Jacobi) / 12ms (GEMM-Jacobi) -- 77-140x slower than cuSOLVER's 105us kernel -- so graphing launch latency away cannot help. Trial 1 (forced route) measured shape0=22011us, geomean 57553us (133x shape-0 regression).
- Fixed a real CUDA-graph gc pitfall: the captured graph's index tensors + eye were gc-freed after capture -> device-side OOB assert on replay in benchmark mode; retaining them in the cache tuple fixed it.
- n=176/352 megakernel path: nsys shows 92.5% is the single mega_eigh_k launch (2173us GPU exec, already ONE launch, occupancy/latency-bound); eager tail (sort+gather+residual gate) is only ~7.5% (~190us on shape1). Attempting to graph the mega+sort+gather PREFIX silently FAILS: the extension's raw <<<>>> launch on the legacy default stream is NOT captured (verified: replay yields wrong eigenvalues, MAX_L_DIFF=1.53). Fixing needs nvcc edits to the kernel launch (brief forbids), and even then the graphable ceiling is only the ~2-3% tail launch-gap.

OPEN directions I did NOT close (manager's call):
1. n=32 is fundamentally cuSOLVER-kernel-bound; the ONLY lever is a FASTER n=32 solver kernel, not a graph. Leader #4 revolutionaryspaces ('submission_eigh_n32_parallel', 37321us) proves n=32 is winnable -- likely a CUSTOM CUDA batched-Jacobi/QL that runs FEWER sweeps or packs more matrices per CTA to raise occupancy (nvcc-heavy; a brief-21/24-style worker). A single fused n=32 megakernel (one CTA/matrix, whole 32x32 in SMEM, ~6 sweeps) would be ~1 launch AND less compute than cuSOLVER's 15-sweep kernel.
2. The n=176/352 eager RESIDUAL-GATE tail (~7.5%/shape1) could be cut in pure torch WITHOUT a graph -- e.g. skip the recon matrix_norm (keep eigr+orth), or fuse the norms -- a small but safe win the megakernel path leaves on the table (separate from graphs).
3. If the megakernel CUDA source were edited to launch on the current stream (c10::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream), the mega+tail prefix WOULD capture and bank the ~2-3% tail; out of scope for a pure-torch brief but viable for an nvcc worker.
4. Graph capture is proven WORKING + kernelguard-CLEAN here, so any future n where a capturable pure-torch path's execution is <= cuSOLVER would win via the self-timing gate already in place.
